news.title: World Cup 2027 qualifiers: Pressure always on big nations - Wales boss Wilkinson
news.lede: Wales head coach Rhian Wilkinson says her side can "absolutely" beat Norway in December's World Cup play-off final. The Norwegians, managed by former Wales boss Gemma Grainger, are ranked 18 places higher than Wales in the world rankings. Wilkinson's side beat Albania in the semi-finals as they bid to qualify for a first World Cup.

news.title: FIFA Technical Study Group Identifies Four Key Areas for African Teams to Improve After 2026 World Cup
news.lede: FIFA’s Technical Study Group has outlined four key areas African national teams must address to improve their competitiveness following their performances at the 2026 FIFA World Cup. The recommendations focus on improving attacking efficiency, pressing higher up the pitch, managing matches more effectively in the closing stages and building on existing defensive strengths. One of the key areas highlighted is the need for African teams to create more goal scoring opportunities inside the penalty area rather than relying heavily on long range efforts. Improving movement, decision making and combinations in the final third could help teams become more clinical in front of goal.

news.title: Women’s football is growing fast — but players still face major gaps
news.lede: Expected global revenue of over $1 billion and new faces at the U17 World Cup show women's football is booming, but a recent report also highlights need for greater structure globally. At first glance, women's football is healthier than ever. A recent report by FIFPRO, football's global players' union, said worldwide revenue is expected to reach over $1bn (€894m) in 2027. The World Cup in Brazil, a first in South America, will be the last with 32 teams and is expected to be the most watched and biggest revenue-generating women's tournament ever.

news.title: FIFA World Cup 2030: Netflix gets all 104 matches in Spain; will fans still be able to watch for free?
news.lede: Imagine settling in to watch a World Cup match, only to discover that your usual television channel no longer carries it. Would you subscribe to a streaming service to catch every game, or stick to whatever is available for free? That is the question Spanish football fans are facing after Netflix secured the rights to all 104 matches of the 2030 FIFA World Cup in Spain and Andorra. Announced on October 13, the deal marks Netflix’s first broadcast of a major men’s international football tournament in Spain.

news.title: 'Possessed' Davidson fills Weir gap as Scots set up glamour Sweden tie
news.lede: Watch the goals as Scotland beat Czechs in World Cup play-off. Scotland stalwart Erin Cuthbert says Lauren Davidson was "like a woman possessed" against the Czech Republic to help Melissa Andreatta's side overcome the absence of Caroline Weir and move closer to the 2027 World Cup. The Brann forward scored the equaliser after the Czech Republic's shock early goal in Paisley as Scotland twice came from behind to set up a tie against heavyweights Sweden for a place in next summer's tournament in Brazil. Scotland needed the industry and spark of the 25-year-old, because they reached the round two play-off without their two big names playing a huge part in the 3-2 win in the second leg for a 5-2 aggregate score.

news.title: Football Australia launches 'Football Unites' multicultural paper at Parliament House
news.lede: The paper celebrates the multicultural story of Australian football, from the migrant community clubs that built the game to the CommBank Socceroos’ FIFA World Cup 2026™ campaign. It also highlights the programs that Football Australia, its Member Federations and partners deliver for culturally diverse communities, supported by the Australian Government, and how football can continue to work with partners to grow that impact. Since the first association football matches were played in Australia in 1880, the game has been shaped by successive waves of migration, with local clubs becoming social and cultural hubs for generations of new arrivals. Today, with nearly two million participants nationwide, football is often the first sporting home for new Australians.

news.title: FIFA proposes €5.5bn football development fund amid Infantino scrutiny
news.lede: FIFA will propose a $6.35 billion (€5.5 billion) four-year development fund, including $25 million (€21.5 million) for each national association, according to news agency Associated Press (AP). On 28 September, FIFA President Gianni Infantino sent the proposal to the heads of football's six continental confederations. The plan is expected to be finalised by the FIFA Council in December and approved at its congress in March, according to a letter reviewed by AP. "Taken together, your submissions confirm broad agreement on the central objective: FIFA's financial success must serve football and all FIFA's 211 member associations," Infantino said in the letter.

news.title: Racism in English football: South Korea’s Asian Games gold medallist and World Cupper allegedly racially abused
news.lede: AP AP https://ss-i.thgim.com/public/incoming/6bim3o/article71582336.ece/alternates/FREE_1200/Britain_EFL_Championship_Soccer_14279.jpg David Davies Swansea City's Eom Ji-Sung, of South Korea, celebrates scoring their first goal of the game during a Sky Bet Championship soccer match between Swansea City and Watford, Tuesday Sept. 1, 2026, in Swansea, Wales. (David Davies/PA via AP) The game between Swansea and Millwall was stopped for about seven minutes as the referee spoke to both coaches, followed by an announcement over the loud speakers at The Den stadium in southeast London. London South Korean international footballer Eom Ji-sung was allegedly racially abused during Swansea City’s 1-0 win at Millwall in England’s second-tier Championship on Tuesday. The incident reportedly took place when the 24-year-old winger was warming up in the second half as a substitute for visitor Swansea.
